children: The power-sector financier’s loan book expands to Rs 6.17 lakh crore, while a contraction in net interest income and higher expenditure weigh on quarterly profitability

REC, formerly known as Rural Electrification Corporation, reported a 21.2 per cent year-on-year decline in consolidated net profit for the September quarter, highlighting a divergence between balance-sheet expansion and earnings performance. The state-owned power-sector financier’s loan portfolio continued to expand, while its board declared a second interim dividend of Rs 3.50 per equity share for FY27.

Consolidated net profit stood at Rs 3,477.73 crore for the quarter ended 30 September 2026, against Rs 4,414.93 crore in the corresponding period a year earlier. Revenue from operations contracted 1 per cent to Rs 15,000.40 crore from Rs 15,152.67 crore, while profit also declined 17.1 per cent sequentially from Rs 4,192.76 crore in the June quarter.

The divergence between lending growth and profitability is also evident in REC’s income profile. Net interest income (NII), which measures the difference between interest earned and interest paid, fell 9 per cent year on year to Rs 5,478 crore from Rs 6,022 crore.

REC’s consolidated total expenses increased 10.46 per cent year on year to Rs 10,619.29 crore from Rs 9,613.44 crore. Total income, meanwhile, declined to Rs 15,010.43 crore from Rs 15,162.38 crore in the year-earlier quarter.

The combination of lower total income and higher expenditure coincided with the contraction in net profit. The reported figures point to a more challenging earnings environment, although the headline numbers alone do not establish the precise contribution of individual cost components.

REC’s loan book increased by Rs 26,537 crore sequentially to Rs 6.17 lakh crore as of 30 September 2026, marking a 5 per cent rise over the preceding quarter. The expansion indicates continued growth in the company’s lending exposure even as quarterly profitability weakened.

The renewable energy portfolio grew 27 per cent year on year to Rs 86,660 crore. Lending to non-power infrastructure and logistics reached Rs 61,637 crore, representing more than 10 per cent of overall loan assets.

REC’s board declared a second interim dividend of Rs 3.50 per equity share with a face value of Rs 10 for FY27. The company fixed 30 October 2026 as the record date for determining shareholder eligibility. Payment is due on or before 21 November 2026.

The proposed merger with Power Finance Corporation (PFC) also advanced through the regulatory process. REC received a no-objection certificate from the Reserve Bank of India on 15 October, subject to the regulator’s conditions. The proposed merger remains contingent on the requisite approvals.
